hooks.text: A space probe slammed into the crushing skies of Venus.
What happens when a spacecraft hits 300 Gs of deceleration?
The first probe to enter Venus was crushed before landing.

title: The Probe That Fell Into Venus
description: Discover how the Soviet Venera 4 probe survived a brutal entry into the crushing atmosphere of Venus in 1967.

beats.text: A space probe slammed into the crushing skies of Venus.
beats.visual: Artist concept of Venus surface and atmosphere, NASA illustration

beats.text: During atmospheric entry, cabin deceleration reached 300 Gs.
beats.visual: Soviet Venera probe model in a museum display

beats.text: Its heat shield endured temperatures soaring up to 11,000 degrees Celsius.
beats.visual: Artist concept of spacecraft atmospheric entry heat shield

beats.text: The probe deployed its parachute at an altitude of about 52 kilometers.
beats.visual: Venus cloud cover Mariner spacecraft photograph

beats.text: It became the first successful spacecraft to perform in situ analysis.
beats.visual: Jodrell Bank Observatory Lovell Telescope dish, 1967

beats.text: Subsequent analysis proved the hull was crushed before reaching the surface.
beats.visual: Venus globe Magellan texture surface mapping

beats.text: That is how a space probe slammed into the crushing skies of Venus.
beats.visual: Venus cloud cover Mariner spacecraft photograph
